newsitem.title: USA: Toastmaster to take Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: Toastmaster to take Q4 charge.

text.p: Toastmaster Inc, in a restructuring move, said Friday it will take a 1996 fourth-quarter charge related to ceasing production at a plant in Boonville, Mo., and reducing its total workforce from 1996 fourth-quarter levels by about 10 percent.

It said the charge is about $4.9 million, after taxes, or $0.65 a share. In a statement, it said only approximately $250,000 of the special charge will impact cash through the payment of expenses related to the restructuring. The remainder will be non-cash, consisting primarily of tooling and inventory writedowns and increases in inventory reserves.

Toastmaster said it found that its kitchen counter-top appliances can be made more price competitive by sourcing them from lower-cost vendors. As a result, it said the Missouri plant will cease production -- a move expected to result in savings ranging from 10 to 30 percent over current costs.

Earlier in January, the appliance maker said it planned to dispose of its environmental products line, citing low margins and low growth potential. The line consists of electric fans, forced air, radiant and ceramic heaters and humidifiers. It said today's announcement also addresses the financial impact of that action as well.

Disposal of the environmental product line is the culmination of the company's decision nearly two years ago to de-emphasize environmental comfort products that collectively accounted for 3.8 percent of total revenues for the year ended December 31, 1995 and less than 3.0 percent of the anticipated total revenues for the year ended December 31, 1996.
Toastmaster said it received several inquiries regarding the sale of the environmental products business, but no substantive discussions regarding this possible sale are currently ongoing.

Though it is ceasing production of certain countertop appliances in Boonville, Mo., it will continue to manufacture kitchen countertop appliances there sold by Toastmaster that are not sourced from other vendors. In addition, a company plant in Macon, Mo., also will make appliances not outsourced.
It said this restructuring is not expected to have any significant impact on the company's time products operations in Laurinburg, N.C.

Toastmaster is continuing to evaluate possible further restructuring measures that might enhance future financial performance. Among strategic initiatives being pursued are additional alliances with companies owning recognizable brand names that will license the use of those names on new products introduced by Toastmaster.
